newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes 475 bln pesos worth of investments.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes 475 bln pesos worth of investments.

text.p: At least 475 billion pesos are likely to be invested in new and ongoing projects in the Philippines this year, according to Trade and Industry Undersecretary Melito Salazar.

The figure is expected to be the overall target of the government's investment promotion agencies, which include the Board of Investments (BOI), the Philippine Economic Zone Authority, the Subic Metropolitan Bay Authority as well as the Securities and Exchange Commission, Salazar said in a report to Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista, which was made public on Thursday.
There were no figures immediately available on the total investments the agencies attracted in 1996.

But the BOI, the government's national agency for investments promotion, attracted 395 billion pesos worth of projects in 1996, surpassing its target of 380 billion pesos for the year, authorities have said.
"BOI aims to use the newly-created Industry Development Council (IDC) to help develop industries by increasing production, productivity and value added in key sectors," Salazar said in his report.
He said the IDC will initially focus on key sectors including emerging export producers like fresh fruits, footwear, leather goods, rubber, fertilizer, copper products and cocochemicals.

The government will also promote industries on the verge of becoming export earners, like pulp and paper, packaging, printing, shipbuilding and ship repair, paints, stainless steel and petrochemicals, Salazar said.
